chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah and Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abdillah ibn Ali al-Hasani, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-'Amri, from al-Husayn ibn Shaddad al-Ju'fi, from Jabir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "The prophets and the sons of the prophets are not killed except by the son of fornication."
ai.seo_question: Who kills the prophets according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* links the lineage of the killers of the prophets—specifically highlighting the slayers of Yahya and Husayn—to the concept of 'walad zin' (sons of fornication), suggesting a spiritual or genealogical marker of illegitimacy. In Shia exegetical tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as biological illegitimacy but as a qualitative trait of those who sever the bond of prophethood and imamate, distinguishing them from the faithful. The narration serves to underscore the continuity of persecution against the Ahl al-Bayt from the time of the prophets to the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn.
